title: Sh Abhinav David Singh & Anr vs State Nct Of Delhi And Anr on 18 May, 2026

paragraphs.text:
$~108
 * IN THE HIGH COURT OF DELHI AT NEW DELHI
 + CRL.M.C. 3885/2026
 SH ABHINAV DAVID SINGH & ANR. .....Petitioners
 Through: Mr. N.L. Singh and Ms. Anita
 Sharma, Advocates.
 Petitioner No.1 in-person.
 Petitioner No.2 via video-
 conferencing.
 versus

 STATE NCT OF DELHI AND ANR .....Respondents
 Through: Ms. Kiran Bairwa, APP for the State.
 SI Rohit, P.S.: Uttam Nagar.
 Ms. Preeti D. Chaudhary and Mr.
 Amit Masih, Advocates for R-2.
 Respondent No.2 in-person.
 CORAM:
 HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ANUP JAIRAM BHAMBHANI
 ORDER

% 18.05.2026
 CRL.M.A. 15762/2026 (exemption)
 Exemption granted, subject to just exceptions.
 The application stands disposed-of.

By way of the present petition filed under section 528 of the
 Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, the petitioners, who are the
 former husband and sister-in-law of the complainant/respondent No.
 2, seek quashing of case FIR No. 0499/2018 dated 07.06.2018
 registered under sections 498-A / 406 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860
 (' IPC ') at P.S.: Uttam Nagar, Delhi.
This is a digitally signed order.

The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 29/05/2026 at 21:12:53

2. The petition is premised on Settlement Agreement dated 05.06.2023
 arrived at through mediation before the Mediation Centre, Dwarka
 Courts, New Delhi; and Divorce Decree dated 19.09.2024, which is
 the culmination of petitions under sections 10A(1) and 10A(2) of the
 Divorce Act, 1869, whereby the parties had sought dissolution of their
 marriage by mutual consent.

3. The petition is supported by affidavits of the petitioners, as also of
 respondent No. 2, alongwith proof of their IDs.
4. Petitioner No.1 as well as respondent No. 2 are present in court.

Petitioner No.2 is present via video-conferencing. Their credentials
 have been verified and they have also been identified by their
 respective counsel.
5. The parties have confirmed that no child was born from the wed-lock.
6. No appeal is stated to have been filed from the divorce decree.

7. Parties also jointly inform the court that petitioner No. 1's mother,
 namely Ms. Sushma Singh and father, namely Mr. Arun Vijay Singh
 have passed-away on 28.04.2021 and 15.01.2024 respectively; and for
 that reason, though named in the FIR, they are not parties to the
 present proceedings.

8. The court has queried Ms. Bhawna Mashih, respondent No. 2, who
 confirms that she has taken divorce by mutual consent; and that a
 settlement agreement has been entered into between the parties; and
 that in full-and-final settlement of all her claims including towards
 maintenance (past, present and future), stridhan, dowry articles,
 jewellery, permanent alimony, etc., she was to receive a sum of Rs.
 30,00,000/-from petitioner No. 1; out of which Rs. 20,00,000/- was



 CRL.M.C. 3885/2026 Page 2 of 3

This is a digitally signed order.

The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 29/05/2026 at 21:12:53
 paid earlier and Rs. 10,00,000/- has been paid in court today, in
 compliance of the terms of the settlement agreement. Respondent No.
 2 confirms that all aspects of the settlement have now been
 performed.

9. Ms. Kiran Bairwa, learned APP confirms that the State has no
 objection to the subject FIR being quashed.

10. In the circumstances, in line with the law laid down by the Supreme
 Court in Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab & Anr. reported as (2012)
 10 SCC 303 as also in Narinder Singh &Ors. vs. State of Punjab &
 Anr. reported as (2014) 6 SCC 466, this court sees no reason why the
 subject FIR and all proceedings emanating therefrom should not be
 quashed. This court is of the view that in light of the settlement
 between the contesting parties, continuing with the subject FIR and all
 subsequent proceedings would be an exercise in futility and would not
 be conducive to peace and harmony between the parties.

11. Accordingly, FIR No. 0499/2018 dated 07.06.2018 registered under
 sections 498-A / 406 of the IPC at P.S.: Uttam Nagar, Delhi is quashed.
 All proceedings arising therefrom also stand closed.
12. Petition stands disposed-of.
13. Pending applications, if any, also stand disposed-of.

ANUP JAIRAM BHAMBHANI, J
 MAY 18, 2026/ak




 CRL.M.C. 3885/2026 Page 3 of 3
